title: Fabrication of Electrochemical-DNA Biosensors for the Reagentless Detection of Nucleic Acids, Proteins and Small Molecules
protocol: Purchase chemically modified probe DNA from a custom oligonucleotide synthesis company.
Dissolve the probe DNA in phosphate buffered saline pH 7.4 to a concentration of 200 μM.
Verify the concentration by measuring absorbance at 260 nm using a spectrophotometer.
Prepare 1 mL of a 10 mM solution of tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphine (TCEP) in distilled, deionized water.
Combine 1 μL of the probe DNA stock solution with 2 μL of TCEP solution and mix gently.
Incubate the mixture for one hour in a dark, refrigerated container.
Dilute the reduced DNA probe solution with 1 mL of buffer to a concentration of 200 nM.
Incubate gold disk electrodes in 200 μL portions of the diluted probe solution.
Prepare at least 2 mL of 2 mM mercaptohexanol in phosphate buffered saline.
Combine 0.05 micron alumina powder with water on a fine polishing cloth.
Polish gold disk electrodes by moving them in a figure eight pattern for approximately three minutes per electrode.
Rinse polished electrodes with DI-water and immerse them into Eppendorf tubes filled with the same.
Sonicate the electrodes for five minutes to remove any residual alumina powder.
Place the electrodes into a 0.5 M sulfuric acid solution.
Attach the electrodes to a potentiostat along with a platinum counter and silver/silver chloride reference electrode.
Run a series of voltammograms to oxidize, reduce, and electrochemically clean their surfaces.
Perform a second electrochemical cleaning in a solution of 0.01 M KCl in 0.1 M sulfuric acid.
Arrange a set of 2 mL Eppendorf tubes in a rack.
Fill each tube with 200 μL of probe DNA solution.
Rinse gold disk electrodes with DI-water.
Immerse the rinsed electrodes in the relevant probe DNA solution for one hour.
Rinse the electrodes again with DI-water.
Immerse the electrodes in 2 mM mercaptohexanol solution.
Store the electrodes in the mercaptohexanol solution in a dark place at room temperature for 3 hours to overnight.
Rinse the sensor with DI-water.
Soak the sensor in buffer for at least ten minutes.
Immerse the sensor in a 100 nM solution of the relevant recognition strand prior to use.
Rinse the sensor quickly with buffer.
Rinse a fresh sensor with DI-water.
Immerse the sensor in a blank sample lacking the target to record the background signal.
Attach the sensor to the working electrode lead of a potentiostat.
Place a platinum counter electrode into the solution.
Place a silver/silver chloride reference electrode into the solution.
Run a square wave measurement from 0 to -0.6 V with an amplitude of 25 mV and a step size of 1 mV.
Save this background measurement.
Move the electrodes to a solution that contains the target DNA molecule of interest.
Equilibrate for 5 to 120 minutes depending on the size, structure, and concentration of the target.
Collect a second square wave voltammagram.
Move the sensor into a container filled with DI-water for 30 s after measurements are complete.
Repeat rinsing the sensor with fresh deionized water two more times.
Squirt the sensor with a steady stream of DI-water for 30 s if needed.
Rinse the sensor in 6 M guanidine hydrochloride or 70% ethanol if analytes resist standard regeneration methods.
Return the sensor to a solution where measurements will be made.
Attach the methylene-blue and thiol-modified DNA probe directly to the gold electrode.
Hybridize the attached probe with a recognition DNA strand conjugated to the relevant antigen.
Transfer the sensor into an Eppendorf tube containing 100 nM of the recognition DNA strand in PBS for 1 hour.
Place the sensor in the blank solution.
Attach it to the working electrode lead of a potentiostat.
Insert a platinum counter electrode and silver/silver chloride reference electrode into the solution.
Perform square wave voltammetry at a frequency of 60 Hz.
Save the background measurement obtained around -0.35 V.
Transfer electrodes to a solution containing the target analyte.
Incubate for 5 to 60 minutes.
Collect a second square wave voltammagram.
Observe changes in peak intensity at -0.35 V related to antibody concentration.
Rinse a fresh sensor with DI-water and immerse it in a blank sample lacking the target to record background signal.
Attach the sensor to the working electrode lead of a potentiostat.
Place a platinum counter and a silver/silver chloride reference into the solution.
Perform square wave voltammetry at an optimal frequency of 200 Hz (or 60 Hz if applicable).
Transfer the electrodes to a solution containing the target analyte, incubate for approximately 5 minutes.
Collect a second square wave voltammagram.
When used to detect DNA using the first architecture, equilibrate at 200 nM target and observe a signal decrease by at least 60%.
After three brief rinses in deionized water, ensure the signal returns within 0.1-5% of its original value.
For antibody detection sensors, expect a signal decrease of 40 to 80% when equilibrated at appropriate conditions.
For aptamer-based cocaine sensors, observe a signal increase up to 200% depending on frequency and surface coverage.
Ensure the best surface coverage for cocaine sensor is low.
